topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture on cancer evolution and outlines the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms driving clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sequential genetic mutations and transient epigenetic alterations confer selective advantages that drive clonal expansion in tissues.

topics.label: Cell of origin and cancer stem cell hierarchy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the parallels between normal stem cells and cancer cells and evaluate experimental evidence for cancer stem cells and cellular hierarchy in leukemias and colorectal cancer.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promoters, chronic inflammation, and stromal dependency
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how microenvironmental factors, inflammatory signals, and supportive stroma permit mutant cells to acquire stem-like properties and sustain malignant growth.

topics.label: Experimental and computational methods for studying tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the modern sequencing, spatial omics, and computational technologies used to investigate tumor evolution and cell-microenvironment interactions.

topics.label: Integrated evolutionary model of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: It synthesizes the interplay among genetic mutations, epigenetics, cell of origin, and microenvironmental conditions into a unified evolutionary model of cancer.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture session and provides a brief preview of the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
